subject: ophthalmology
title: Diseases of the conjunctiva

steps.tx: **Acute bacterial conjunctivitis** glues lids with mucopurulent discharge (staphylococcal, streptococcal, Haemophilus in children), while **viral disease** (adenovirus) waters with follicles, preauricular nodes, recent upper respiratory contact and cross infectivity; membranes or pseudomembranes mark severe adenoviral or streptococcal variants. Gonococcal conjunctivitis is hyperacute with copious pus and corneal perforation risk in neonates and adults, needing systemic ceftriaxone plus lavage. Chlamydial inclusion conjunctivitis causes chronic follicular disease with mucopurulent discharge in sexually active adults (treat partners with azithromycin).
steps.say: Pus that glues is bacterial; water with nodes is viral. Hyperacute pus that melts cornea is gonococcus: inject ceftriaxone.

steps.tx: **Trachoma** (Chlamydia trachomatis serotypes A to C) blinds through repeated childhood infection scarring lids inward: McCallan stages run follicular activity to cicatricial quiet, while WHO FISTO grades follicles, intense inflammation, scarring, trichiasis and corneal opacity. Diagnosis needs upper tarsal follicles with pannus, Herbert pits or stellate scarring. The **SAFE** strategy (surgery for trichiasis, antibiotics with single dose azithromycin, facial cleanliness, environmental improvement) eliminates blinding disease; trichiasis surgery (bilamellar tarsal rotation) precedes corneal opacity.
steps.say: Upper lid follicles plus pannus is trachoma. SAFE with azithromycin stops villages going blind.

steps.tx: **Allergic conjunctivitis** itches with ropy discharge and papillae: seasonal hay fever type, perennial dust mite type, and **vernal keratoconjunctivitis** in atopic boys with giant cobblestone papillae, Trantas dots and shield ulcers threatening vision. Management avoids rubbing, cools with lubricants, mast cell stabilisers and antihistamines, reserving short steroids or ciclosporin and supratarsal injections for shield disease. Atopic keratoconjunctivitis scars lids chronically. Contact lens overwear breeds giant papillary conjunctivitis with mucus and lens intolerance, eased by lens holiday and fit change.
steps.say: Itch dominates allergy; giant papillae in atopic boys is vernal. Shield ulcer in vernal disease threatens sight.

steps.tx: Degenerative and surface disease: **pinguecula** is a benign yellow nasal nodule that never crosses limbus, while **pterygium** is a wing shaped growth invading cornea (UV driven), needing excision with autograft when encroaching. **Dry eye** burns with fluctuating vision, low tear breakup time and punctate staining, managed by preservative free tears, punctal plugs and ciclosporin; Sjogren, Stevens Johnson and chemical burns need specialist care. Bitot spots (foamy patches) flag vitamin A deficiency in malnourished children.
steps.say: Pinguecula stops at limbus, pterygium flies onto cornea. Foamy Bitot spots mean vitamin A deficiency.
